subject: Biology
title: Classification of Living Organisms
description: How living organisms are grouped into major classification categories.

questions.prompt: The process of grouping living organisms based on shared characteristics is called:
Animals that have a backbone are called:
Animals without a backbone, such as insects and worms, are called:
Which of these is a characteristic of mammals?
options: They lay eggs and have scales
They have fur/hair and feed young with milk

questions.prompt: Which of these is a characteristic shared by all birds?
options: They have feathers and most can fly

questions.prompt: Name three major groups of vertebrates and give one distinguishing characteristic of each.
questions.rubricGuidance: Accept any three of: mammals (fur, milk), birds (feathers, most fly), reptiles (scales, cold-blooded), amphibians (moist skin, live in water and land), fish (gills, fins, live in water).

expectedPoints.text: Amphibians (moist skin, live in water and land)

questions.prompt: Explain why scientists classify living organisms, and describe the main groups of vertebrates and invertebrates with their key distinguishing features.

keyPoints.text: Classification groups organisms based on shared characteristics, making them easier to study and identify
Vertebrates are animals with a backbone, including fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals
Invertebrates are animals without a backbone, including insects, worms, and molluscs
Fish live in water, breathe through gills, and typically have fins and scales
Amphibians can live both in water and on land and typically have moist skin
Reptiles have dry, scaly skin and are typically cold-blooded
Birds have feathers, lay eggs, and most are capable of flight
Mammals have fur or hair and feed their young with milk
